exposure: presenting symptoms (fever, cough, dyspnea, upper respiratory symptoms, fatigue, diarrhea, loss of smell)
clinical conditions (upper respiratory tract infection, abnormal chest X-ray, lymphopenia, high inflammatory markers, end organ damage)
cohort: 99 confirmed hospitalized COVID-19 patients admitted to King Saud University Medical City (KSUMC) in Riyadh, KSA, between March 22 and May 31, 2020.
finding: The study found no MERS-CoV co-infection among the hospitalized COVID-19 patients and identified late presentation with severe disease, abnormal chest X-ray, lymphopenia, high inflammatory markers, and end organ damage as predictors for critical care admission or death.
